propositions: The false_accept computation in _recall_false_accept counts safe gold items NOT blocked, but is consumed at two sites as if it counts safe items that WERE blocked, inverting the metric semantics.

A candidate that false-fires on fewer safe items than baseline is incorrectly failed with 'false-accept rose' under the inverted metric, as evidenced by the recorded frontier slot failure (0.143 rise reported for 0.143 improvement).
The max_false_accept ceiling of 0.10 at parity.py:230 is effectively always-fail for any competent gate because it compares against the inverted metric (specificity>0.10 instead of error-rate<0.10).

The metric name false_accept and lower-is-better semantics are already established elsewhere in the codebase (evals/eval.py:399,491; plan-review-gate.md:382; container eval yaml), so the fix is to correct the computation, not rename or invert comparisons.
Correcting the computation from 'not blocked' to 'blocked' over safe items and updating docstring leaves both comparison operators unchanged, converging multiple artifacts on a single definition.

The fixture fidelity_spot_eval.py contains conflicting labels (advisory gold vs must-block comment) that were only survivable because the inverted metric vacuously scored 0.0; corrected labels expose the real false-accept criterion.
